## Synthetic data

This project contains synthetic data and analysis created for demonstration
purposes only. Helix Therapeutics and study HLX-301 are fictional. No real
subject data, site data, or trial data went into this report.
:::

::: {.callout-note}
## AI-generated content

AI wrote the commentary and the clinical scenarios in this report, as an
illustration. No subject-matter expert reviewed them.
:::

```{python}
# | label: setup
import json
import os
import re

import awswrangler as wr
import boto3
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import pandas as pd
from great_tables import GT, loc, style

# This report goes to Posit Connect as a self-contained document. It does not
# import config.py from the repository, because the bundle does not hold that
# file. The settings it needs are below. Each one reads an environment variable
# first, so Connect can point the report at another account.
# tests/test_report_config.py makes sure these agree with config.py.
REGION = os.environ.get("POSIT_DEMO_REGION", "us-east-2")
WORKGROUP = os.environ.get("POSIT_DEMO_WORKGROUP", "primary")
DATABASE = os.environ.get("POSIT_DEMO_DATABASE", "helix_trials")
ENDPOINT = os.environ.get("POSIT_DEMO_ENDPOINT", "helix-dropout-risk")
BUCKET_PREFIX = "sagemaker-posit-conf-2026-demo"

session = boto3.Session(region_name=REGION)

# This report asks STS for the account number, and does not store it. This
# public repository therefore holds no account number, and a fork needs no edit.
BUCKET = os.environ.get("POSIT_DEMO_BUCKET") or (
    f"{BUCKET_PREFIX}-"
    f"{session.client('sts').get_caller_identity()['Account']}-{REGION}"
)
ATHENA_STAGING = f"s3://{BUCKET}/athena-query-results/"

plt.rcParams.update({
    "figure.dpi": 140, "axes.spines.top": False, "axes.spines.right": False,
    "axes.grid": True, "grid.alpha": 0.25, "font.size": 9,
})
POSIT_BLUE, POSIT_ORANGE, POSIT_BURGUNDY = "#447099", "#ee6331", "#9a4665"


def athena(sql: str) -> pd.DataFrame:
    return wr.athena.read_sql_query(
        sql,
        database=DATABASE,
        workgroup=WORKGROUP,
        s3_output=ATHENA_STAGING,
        boto3_session=session,
        # ctas_approach=False: the default creates temporary Glue tables, which
        # needs Glue write permission the read-only demo role does not have.
        ctas_approach=False,
    )
```

```{python}
# | label: load
# Group the visit history over a fixed early window first, Screening to Week
# 12, and then join to the subject table. If you join on a later visit first,
# the query removes every subject who already withdrew. That is survivorship
# bias, and it reports a dropout rate far below the true one.
subjects = athena("""
    WITH early_window AS (
        SELECT subject_id,
               count(*)                                                  AS early_visits,
               CAST(sum(CASE WHEN NOT visit_completed THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS double)
                   / count(*)                                            AS missed_visit_rate
        FROM fct_visit_observations
        WHERE visit_id <= 5
        GROUP BY subject_id
    )
    SELECT s.subject_id, s.arm, s.age, s.sex, s.ecog_status, s.bmi,
           s.prior_therapy_lines, s.baseline_das, s.early_ae_count,
           w.missed_visit_rate, s.discontinued,
           t.site_name, t.country, t.region
    FROM dim_subject s
    JOIN early_window w ON w.subject_id = s.subject_id
    JOIN dim_site t     ON t.site_id    = s.site_id
""")

das = athena("""
    SELECT v.visit_name, v.scheduled_day, s.arm,
           avg(o.das_score) AS mean_das,
           count(*)         AS observations
    FROM fct_visit_observations o
    JOIN dim_subject s ON s.subject_id = o.subject_id
    JOIN dim_visit   v ON v.visit_id   = o.visit_id
    WHERE v.scheduled_day >= 0
    GROUP BY v.visit_name, v.scheduled_day, s.arm
    ORDER BY v.scheduled_day
""")

n_subjects = len(subjects)
n_sites = subjects["site_name"].nunique()
discont_rate = subjects["discontinued"].mean()
```

## Study status

**`{python} f"{n_subjects:,}"`** subjects are randomized across
**`{python} n_sites`** active sites in
**`{python} subjects["region"].nunique()`** regions. Overall early
discontinuation stands at **`{python} f"{discont_rate*100:.1f}%"`**.

This report reads the data from Amazon Athena each time it renders.

```{python}
# | label: tbl-arms
arms = (
    subjects.groupby("arm")
    .agg(subjects=("subject_id", "size"),
         mean_age=("age", "mean"),
         baseline_das=("baseline_das", "mean"),
         early_ae=("early_ae_count", "mean"),
         discontinued=("discontinued", "mean"))
    .reset_index()
)

(
    GT(arms)
    .tab_header(title="Balance and retention by treatment arm",
                subtitle="Discontinuation computed over all randomized subjects")
    .cols_label(arm="Arm", subjects="Subjects", mean_age="Mean age",
                baseline_das="Baseline DAS", early_ae="Mean AEs to Wk 12",
                discontinued="Discontinued")
    .fmt_number(columns="subjects", decimals=0, use_seps=True)
    .fmt_number(columns=["mean_age", "baseline_das", "early_ae"], decimals=2)
    .fmt_percent(columns="discontinued", decimals=1)
    .tab_style(style=style.text(weight="bold"), locations=loc.column_labels())
    .tab_source_note("Synthetic data, generated for demonstration purposes.")
)
```

The two arms are balanced on age and on baseline disease activity. By Week 12
the treatment arm records more adverse events, and it also loses more subjects.
This is the expected trade-off for an active drug.

## Efficacy and safety

```{python}
# | label: fig-efficacy
# | fig-cap: "Disease activity trajectory by arm, and discontinuation against early adverse-event burden."
fig, (ax1, ax2) = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(10, 4))

for arm, color in (("Treatment", POSIT_BLUE), ("Placebo", POSIT_ORANGE)):
    part = das[das["arm"] == arm].sort_values("scheduled_day")
    ax1.plot(part["scheduled_day"], part["mean_das"], marker="o",
             linewidth=1.8, label=arm, color=color)
ax1.set(title="Mean disease activity score (lower is better)",
        xlabel="study day", ylabel="DAS")
ax1.legend(frameon=False)

by_ae = subjects.groupby("early_ae_count")["discontinued"].mean() * 100
by_ae.plot.bar(ax=ax2, color=POSIT_BURGUNDY, rot=0, width=0.72)
ax2.set(title="Discontinuation by AE burden to Week 12",
        xlabel="adverse events recorded", ylabel="discontinued (%)")

fig.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

```{python}
# | label: efficacy-text
# | output: asis
wk24 = das[das["scheduled_day"] == 168].set_index("arm")["mean_das"]
if {"Treatment", "Placebo"} <= set(wk24.index):
    sep = wk24["Placebo"] - wk24["Treatment"]
    print(
        f"At Week 24 the treatment arm is at **{wk24['Treatment']:.2f}** and "
        f"placebo is at **{wk24['Placebo']:.2f}**. The gap is "
        f"**{sep:.2f} DAS points**, and it holds to the end of the study.\n\n"
        f"Discontinuation rises quickly as early adverse events increase. This "
        f"is where a study team can act. The adverse event count at Week 12 is "
        f"visible long before a subject withdraws."
    )
```

## Dropout risk

```{python}
# | label: score
# | output: false
FEATURES = ["age", "ecog_status", "bmi", "prior_therapy_lines",
            "baseline_das", "early_ae_count", "missed_visit_rate", "arm"]

endpoint_available = True
endpoint_error = ""

# The endpoint exists only around the time of a session. If it is gone, this
# report must still render on Connect. The error is therefore stored and shown
# on the page, and the render continues.
try:
    body = json.dumps({"instances": subjects[FEATURES].to_dict(orient="records")})
    response = session.client("sagemaker-runtime").invoke_endpoint(
        EndpointName=ENDPOINT, ContentType="application/json", Body=body
    )
    subjects["dropout_risk"] = json.loads(response["Body"].read())["predictions"]
except Exception as err:  # noqa: BLE001
    endpoint_available = False
    # AWS error text repeats the account number. This report gets published,
    # so the number is masked before it reaches the page.
    endpoint_error = re.sub(
        r"\b\d{12}\b", "<account>", f"{type(err).__name__}: {err}"
    )
```

```{python}
# | label: score-note
# | output: asis
if not endpoint_available:
    print(":::: {.callout-warning}\n")

        "section is omitted. Everything above is queried directly from Athena "
        "and is unaffected.\n"
    )
    print(
        f"Deploy it with `uv run python ml/train_and_deploy.py --domain "
        f"{"lifesci"}`, then re-render.\n"
    )
    print(f"> `{endpoint_error}`\n")
    print("::::\n")
```

```{python}
# | label: tbl-sites
if endpoint_available:
    watchlist = (
        subjects.groupby(["region", "site_name"])
        .agg(enrolled=("subject_id", "size"),
             predicted=("dropout_risk", "mean"),
             actual=("discontinued", "mean"))
        .query("enrolled >= 20")
        .sort_values("predicted", ascending=False)
        .head(10)
        .reset_index()
    )
    out = (
        GT(watchlist)
        .tab_header(title="Sites with the highest predicted dropout risk",
                    subtitle="Sites with at least 20 subjects enrolled")
        .cols_label(region="Region", site_name="Site", enrolled="Enrolled",
                    predicted="Predicted risk", actual="Discontinued to date")
        .fmt_number(columns="enrolled", decimals=0)
        .fmt_percent(columns=["predicted", "actual"], decimals=1)
        .data_color(columns="predicted", palette=["#ffffff", POSIT_BURGUNDY])
        .tab_style(style=style.text(weight="bold"), locations=loc.column_labels())
        .tab_source_note(f"Scored on endpoint {ENDPOINT}. "
                         "Synthetic data, generated for demonstration purposes.")
    )
else:
    out = None
out
```

```{python}
# | label: summary
# | output: asis
if endpoint_available:
    flagged = subjects.nlargest(50, "dropout_risk")
    hit = flagged["discontinued"].mean() * 100
    base = discont_rate * 100
    print(
        f"Sort every subject by predicted risk. The 50 highest show a "
        f"**{hit:.0f}%** discontinuation rate, against **{base:.1f}%** for the "
        f"whole study. That is **{hit/base:.1f}** times the study rate, and a "
        f"list of 50 is short enough for a study manager to work through site "
        f"by site.\n\n"
        f"The two strongest drivers are the adverse event count and the missed "
        f"visits in the first 12 weeks. Every site already records both, so no "
        f"new data collection is necessary."
    )
```

## Method

A script makes the data. The data goes to Amazon S3 as parquet, and the tables
are registered in the AWS Glue Data Catalog.

This report reads those tables through Amazon Athena when it renders. It then
scores every subject against a logistic dropout-risk model. Amazon SageMaker
hosts that model on a real-time endpoint.

Every step runs from Positron on Amazon SageMaker, and the report is published
to Posit Connect.

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true"}
## Build this report again

```bash
uv run python data/generate.py     --domain lifesci
uv run python load/load_athena.py  --domain lifesci
uv run python ml/train_and_deploy.py --domain lifesci
quarto render reports/helix_trials/enrollment_safety_review.qmd
uv run python ml/teardown.py --all
```
:::
